notes: All 6 required web searches ran this time, plus 2 follow-ups (8 in total); none were refused, so the earlier note about an incomplete search no longer applies. The only AI-risk statement found is from his own X post (18 September 2026), seen through the Digg AI aggregator page, not opened at X (x.com returned HTTP 402). Two separate fetches of the Digg page agreed on the phrase 'sensible regulation to eliminate catastrophic risk' and on the opening 'Grateful to cosponsor @GOPPolicy Chairman @JayObernolte's Frontier Act which is a smart bipartisan framework'; one fetch also gave the fuller 'a smart bipartisan framework to spur continued AI innovation with sensible regulation to eliminate catastrophic risk', but I could not confirm that this is one continuous passage, so only the short phrase is quoted. Because the source is an X post, the separate X collection may already have it; the reviewer should check the post text there and avoid counting it twice. Frontier Act co-sponsorship: the Obernolte/Trahan release (23 July 2026, via Quiver Quantitative) names only the original sponsors and not Wilson; Congress.gov returned HTTP 403, so his co-sponsorship rests only on his own post. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, Casar, September 2026): search results describe its House co-sponsors as Democrats and none mention Wilson, but no full co-sponsor list could be opened (Congress.gov and GovTrack returned 403), so this is not confirmed either way. No House letter on AI risk led by him was found. Search results naming Alan Wilson (South Carolina attorney general) on the 2025 state AI law moratorium concern a different person and were left out. Kept from the earlier attempt: his press-release pages 1 to 4 (about 40 releases, 8 January 2025 to 26 October 2026) contained nothing about AI, and the 5 June 2026 FY27 NDAA release does not mention AI; page 1 was rechecked this time with the same result.
